guards.what: G2 (LIVE, promoted from the prior round's DORMANT): CardSelectorPrefs' `Cancelable = false` and the min-0/max-3 range, vs the driver's non-skippable, always-fill-count selection loop
guards.issue: Closed 2026-08-01 (tier-2 round 13): FIXED. C#'s Kifuda.cs:24-37 builds CardSelectorPrefs(EnchantSelectionPrompt, 0, Cards.IntValue) with Cancelable = false and RequireManualConfirmation = true -- MinSelect 0, MaxSelect 3, so the player may confirm having enchanted FEWER than 3 but may not back out. The sim now expresses that: a new `enchant_optional` purpose in driver.SKIPPABLE_PURPOSES makes the picks declinable while the screen as a whole stays non-skippable (confirming 0 and backing out are DIFFERENT things). Mutation-verified: 8 of the 13 new pins fail with the mechanism disabled; the 5 survivors are the intended controls. CAVEAT ON RECORD (round-13 review): the 0..3 range is the PREFS range the automated selector arm operates at, NOT a literal description of the shipped single-player screen, whose ConfirmSelection (NDeckEnchantSelectScreen.cs:258-264) refuses a 0-card finalize and whose only zero-card exit is gated behind Cancelable. The sim deliberately models the prefs range because it sits at the ICardSelector/driver abstraction. THE MECHANISM relic/_auto_keep DOES NOT CLOSE -- see relic/gnarled_hammer. WHAT REASONING THIS REPLACES: the premise that the port 'does nothing at all' (stale -- the pickup was fully implemented; only the partial confirm was missing).  The text it replaced read: PROMOTED 2026-07-30 (round 11): G1 was closed 2026-07-29 (after_obtained is now implemented), which discharges the prior round's own stated precondition for dormancy ('it stays dormant until G1 is fixed: with the relic implementing nothing, there is no screen to get wrong'). Re-executed against the now-real implementation rather than inherited. MECHANISM: Kifuda.cs:26 is `new CardSelectorPrefs(EnchantSelectionPrompt, 0, base.DynamicVars.Cards.IntValue) { Cancelable = false, RequireManualConfirmation = true }` -- confirmed by reading the source directly -- i.e. MinSelect=0, MaxSelect=3: the player may confirm the screen having enchanted 0, 1 or 2 cards even when 3 or more are eligible; they may only not back out of the screen entirely. kifuda.py:25 is `run.select_cards("enchant", candidates, self.CARDS)` (self.CARDS == 3). `RunState.select_cards` (run.py:488-507) itself is permissive -- EXECUTED (`.superpowers/sdd/unlabelled/probes/relic-7-kifuda-g2.py`): a hand-rolled `card_selector` installed directly on a bare `RunState` that always returns only 1 candidate IS honoured (`enchanted count when selector tries to return only 1: 1`), so the restriction is not in `run.select_cards`. It is in the driver actually used by gameplay/the RL environment: `RunDriver._card_selector` (driver.py:329-350) checks `skippable = purpose in SKIPPABLE_PURPOSES` (driver.py:93-96), and `"enchant"` is NOT a member; with `skippable=False`, `DecisionRequest.legal_actions()` for SELECT_CARDS is `list(range(len(candidates)))` with no append of the skip index (driver.py:221-225) -- there is no legal action that means 'stop early'. The `_card_selector` loop (driver.py:335-349) then runs exactly `count` iterations whenever `count < len(remaining)`, so the policy is offered zero, one, two... but never allowed to end the picking before 3 selections are made. OBSERVABLE, EXECUTED: same probe -- `run.select_cards` with no selector attached enchants exactly 3 of the starting Ironclad deck's 10 cards (`enchanted count (no selector installed): 3`, `['strike','strike','defend']`) and `'enchant' in SKIPPABLE_PURPOSES: False`. TRIGGER: kifuda.py:25, reached by any run that buys Kifuda (Shop rarity) while at least one eligible card is in the deck -- true of essentially every run (the bare starting deck alone has 8 of 10 cards eligible: 5 Strike + 4 Defend, minus nothing, since none carry Status/Curse/Quest or an existing enchantment). FIX: give `RunState.select_cards`/`RunDriver._card_selector` a MinSelect-aware partial-stop action -- e.g. replace the boolean `SKIPPABLE_PURPOSES` with a per-purpose minimum, and append the stop action to `legal_actions()` once `len(picked) >= min_select` rather than only when the whole purpose is fully skippable. RADIUS: `sts2_rl/driver.py`'s `SKIPPABLE_PURPOSES` / `_card_selector` / `DecisionRequest.legal_actions` are shared machinery reused by every out-of-combat card-selection purpose (transform, upgrade, remove, and every other enchant relic); not independently re-checked for beautiful_bracelet, electric_shrymp or paels_growth here -- electric_shrymp's own N2 and tri_boomerang's own N3 record that THEIR C# `CardSelectorPrefs` constructors set `MinSelect == MaxSelect` (a forced-exact-count screen with no player choice to remove), which is a DIFFERENT shape from Kifuda's genuine 0..3 range, so this finding does not mechanically extend to them without independently reading beautiful_bracelet.cs/paels_growth.cs's own constructor call (HANDOFF candidate, not claimed here). The issue it replaced read: C# offers a not-cancelable screen whose selection size is 0..3 -- the player may confirm with fewer than 3 picks but may not back out -- while the sim's out-of-combat verb is `run.select_cards(purpose, candidates, count)` (run.py:371-390), which takes ONE count and has no min/max range or cancelable flag. Its default policy returns exactly `min(count, len(candidates))` picks. So a fixed port would enchant exactly 3 whenever 3 cards are eligible, where C# lets a player enchant 1. DORMANT and it stays dormant until G1 is fixed: with the relic implementing nothing, there is no screen to get wrong.
